---
description: "How Island Transit's on-time record compares with other bus systems, adjusted for their different definitions of on time."
title: "Compared with other bus systems"
subtitle: "Each agency's figure on the same footing as ours"
---

Bus agencies don't all mean the same thing by "on time." One counts a bus up
to 5 minutes late, another only up to 3, and some time arrivals at every
stop while others time departures at a few. So two published percentages
can't be set side by side as they are: a stricter rule makes the same buses
look worse. Below, each agency's own figure is put on the same footing as
ours in one of two ways, and each row says which.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {json, pct, count, longDate, emptyNote, guard, h} from "./lib.js"
import {makeCharts} from "./charts.js"
import {Plot} from "./vendor/plot-0.6.11/plot.js"
ch = makeCharts({Plot})
cmp = json("data/compare/summary.json")
peers = (cmp?.peers ?? []).filter(p => p && p.agency)
it = cmp?.island_transit ?? null
// A peer with no window either measures something else (headways, waiting
// time) or published nothing we could find.
rule = p => p.window != null ? `${p.window[0] ?? 0} min early to ${p.window[1]} min late`
  : /headway|wait/i.test(`${p.measured} ${p.note}`) ? "not a punctuality window" : "rule not found"
```

The first way recounts our own departures under the other agency's rule
(marked R). That shows how Island Transit would score if it used that
agency's definition. The second turns the other agency's published figure
into a figure under our rule, 1 minute early to 5 minutes late (marked B).
We don't have the other agency's departure times, so we assume its buses
run early and late in a pattern like ours, only wider or narrower, and try
several such patterns. The result is a range, not a single number, and a
wide range means the answer depends a lot on that assumption.

A few agencies publish their own live bus locations, as Island Transit
does. For those, we also run our own method on two hours of their buses
once a week (marked A) and report the share on time under our rule, with a
range that allows for chance. Two hours on one day is a small slice of
their service, so treat it as a spot check.

::: {.slot-chart}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!cmp || !it) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The comparisons");
  const rows = peers.filter(p => p.converted_to_our_window?.low != null)
    .map(p => ({name: `${p.agency} (${p.country})`, lo: p.converted_to_our_window.low, hi: p.converted_to_our_window.high}));
  const ours = it.recount_under_our_rule;
  if (rows.length === 0) return html`<p class="empty">No other agency's figure could be converted yet.</p>`;
  const all = [{name: "Island Transit (ours)", lo: ours, hi: ours, us: true}, ...rows];
  return ch.figure({
    title: "On time under our rule, 1 minute early to 5 minutes late",
    note: `Island Transit: ${pct(ours, 1)} of ${count(it.departures)} departures at timepoints from ${longDate(it.first_service_date)} to ${longDate(it.last_service_date)}, with every moment counted alike. Each bar spans the converted figure under the assumptions tried.`,
    chart: ch.responsive((width, narrow) => Plot.plot({
      ariaLabel: "Converted on-time shares of other bus systems, beside Island Transit's",
      ariaDescription: all.map(d => `${d.name}: ${d.us ? pct(d.lo, 1) : `${pct(d.lo)} to ${pct(d.hi)}`}`).join("; "),
      style: {background: "transparent", fontSize: "12px", overflow: "visible"},
      width, height: 34 * all.length + 50,
      marginLeft: narrow ? 6 : Math.min(320, 14 + 6.6 * Math.max(...all.map(d => d.name.length))), marginRight: 30, marginTop: narrow ? 24 : 8, marginBottom: 36,
      x: {domain: [0, 1], grid: true, tickFormat: d => pct(d), label: null},
      y: {domain: all.map(d => d.name), label: null, axis: narrow ? null : "left", tickSize: 0},
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY(all, {y: "name", x1: "lo", x2: "hi", stroke: "var(--range)", strokeWidth: 6, strokeLinecap: "round"}),
        Plot.dot(all.filter(d => d.us), {y: "name", x: "lo", r: 6, fill: "var(--series-1)", stroke: "var(--surface)", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
        narrow ? Plot.text(all, {y: "name", x: 0, text: "name", textAnchor: "start", dy: -16, fill: "currentColor"}) : null,
        Plot.tip(all, Plot.pointerY({y: "name", x: "hi", title: d => d.us ? `${d.name}\n${pct(d.lo, 1)}` : `${d.name}\n${pct(d.lo)} to ${pct(d.hi)} under our rule`})),
      ],
    }), {height: 34 * all.length + 50}),
    methods: "comparisons",
  });
}, "The comparison chart")
```
:::

## Every agency we looked at

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (!cmp) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The comparison table");
  const rows = peers.map(p => ({
    ...p,
    theirRule: rule(p) + (p.window != null && p.measured ? `, ${p.measured}` : ""),
    theirs: p.published_share,
    ourUnderTheirs: p.island_under_their_rule ?? null,
    range: p.converted_to_our_window?.low == null ? null : `${pct(p.converted_to_our_window.low)} to ${pct(p.converted_to_our_window.high)}`,
    how: p.classes?.length ? p.classes.join(", ") : "published only",
    sampled: p.our_method_on_their_feed ?? null,
  }));
  return html`${ch.table(rows, {
    caption: "Other bus systems' on-time rules and figures, and how they compare",
    wide: true,
    columns: [
      {key: "agency", label: "Agency", format: (v, r) => r.sources?.[0] ? h("a", {href: r.sources[0]}, v) : v},
      {key: "region", label: "Where"},
      {key: "theirRule", label: "Their rule"},
      {key: "theirs", label: "Their figure", align: "right", format: (v, r) => v == null ? "–" : `${pct(v, 1)}${r.published_period ? ` (${r.published_period})` : ""}`},
      {key: "ourUnderTheirs", label: "Island Transit under their rule (R)", align: "right", format: v => v == null ? "–" : pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "range", label: "Theirs under our rule (B)", align: "right", sortValue: r => r.converted_to_our_window?.low ?? null},
      {key: "sampled", label: "Their buses, our method (A)", align: "right", sortValue: r => r.sampled?.on_time_share ?? null,
       format: v => v?.on_time_share == null ? "–" : `${pct(v.on_time_share)}${Array.isArray(v.on_time_interval_95) && v.on_time_interval_95.every(Number.isFinite) ? ` (${pct(v.on_time_interval_95[0])} to ${pct(v.on_time_interval_95[1])})` : ""}${v.service_date ? `, ${longDate(v.service_date)}` : ""}`},
      {key: "how", label: "Compared by"},
      {key: "confidence", label: "Source"},
    ],
  })}
  <p class="note">"Source" says how firm the published rule and figure are: high when an official source states both. Rules that don't use a window, such as the excess wait time some cities use for frequent buses, can't be compared this way and are listed as published only.</p>`;
}, "The comparison table")
```

These comparisons are rough by nature. They can't adjust for differences in
what each agency times (a departure or an arrival), at which stops, or how
it counts a trip that never ran, and the agencies' figures cover different
periods from ours. Each row links to the agency's own report.
